text: Archpriest Andria Jagmaidze - The candidate must be no more than 70 years old; as for education, when a person applies for a job, will they say, "I don't have a diploma, but I am educated"?! - The Synod must be strictly guided by the Statute of Management and Administration (28.04.2026, 11:40)

"In the criteria, we read that he must be Georgian, he must be a monk, he must be a member of the Synod, he must have an education, and there is a reference to age, that he must have reached 40 years of age and be no more than 70 years old - this Synod does not have the right to change the Statute of Management and Administration and must be strictly guided by the Statute of Management and Administration," stated Archpriest Andria Jagmaidze, the head of the Public Relations Department of the Patriarchate.
According to him, it is important for the life of the church that a defined rule be observed.
"Today, the selection of three patriarchal candidates will take place at the Synod, and the subsequent Synod, an expanded session, will be for the election of the Patriarch."

In the criteria, we read that he must be Georgian, he must be a monk, he must be a member of the Synod, he must have an education, and there is a reference to age, stating that he must have reached 40 years of age and be no more than 70 years old.

I am a mathematician, the phrase "not more than 70 years" means that adding any amount of time to 70 is no longer "not more than 70". That is, 70 plus some days and months is already more than 70; as a mathematician, for me, this is crystal clear, however, let's see what decision the Synod will make on this.

The second is that this Synod does not have the right to change the Statute of Management and Administration and must be guided strictly by the Statute of Management and Administration. As for the topic of education, how do you imagine it, when a person does not have a diploma and applies for a job vacancy, what will they say—that I don't have a diploma, but I am an educated person?! This will not work in any job.

Every issue can be subject to interpretation, for example, the question could be raised, what it means to be Georgian. I had a friend, a Yezidi, and internally he was a very good Georgian, now if we judge this way, everything can be called into question. There is also such a concept as “hidden monks” and now here in the criteria it says monk - “hidden monk” means that they are not tonsured, but live a monastic life, in other words, everything can be subject to interpretation. So, I think, it is very important for the life of the church, that the rule, which is defined, be upheld.
"We have already received information about the delegates from most of the dioceses," stated Andria Jaghmaidze.
